intent: A vertical milestone rail with numbered checkpoints, an animated completion rule and focused stage notes for reviews, onboarding and handovers.

layout.direction: A focused sprint progress card with a compact heading and completed-stage count, a fine drawn completion rail and numbered stage actions. Completed circles become checkmarks; the current stage points toward a written detail below. Keep neutral graphite surfaces, 14px stage labels, 12px counts, 44px targets and 3:1 control boundaries. Long labels and details wrap naturally.
layout.container: Full-width progress card capped at 576px with 24px padding at every width. The separate centred demo stage has a 620px minimum height and 16px padding, rising to 32px at the sm viewport breakpoint.
layout.longContent: Keep the header count in one non-shrinking block, allow the title to wrap, and give multiline stage buttons 8px vertical inner space with 44px minimum targets.

typography.metadata: 12px monospaced counts and editorial labels where present
typography.heading: 20px medium sans-serif

motion.entrance: Enter the card with opacity and an 8px rise over 320ms. Draw the first completion fill from zero over 350ms after a 160ms delay.
motion.interaction: Later completion changes animate both directions over 350ms. Key actual stage details and enter them with opacity and a 4px rise over 240ms. Keep 150ms stage-button feedback.
motion.reduced: Subscribe to live prefers-reduced-motion changes and stop and settle owned card, fill and detail controls immediately. Remove press transforms.

responsive.rules: Wrap long copy; stack secondary details inside narrow containers; keep any horizontal scrolling local and keyboard accessible.

accessibility: Use native buttons and form controls with visible 2px focus rings.
Provide labels, meaningful states and polite feedback where actions update content.
Keep IDs instance-scoped with useId; support multiple instances and empty custom data.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion; no automatic action or navigation.

content.defaults: Use the realistic default content from the source; expose content and collection inputs as typed props.

props.name: steps
props.description: Ordered stages with stable unique IDs, labels and plain-text details. ID keys retain focused stages through reordering.

props.name: current
props.description: Zero-based current index, clamped to the supplied stages. steps.length means all complete; invalid or negative values start at zero. The host owns this value.

props.name: onStepChange
props.description: Synchronous host navigation request with the clicked current-order index. Without it, stages are read-only. A request does not advance the host value automatically.

props.name: theme
props.description: Surface and ink palette; the demo stage follows the chosen theme.

avoid: Remote images, fake network success or hidden external dependencies.
Decorative status badges, gradients as filler, low-contrast text.
Unlabelled controls, hover-only functionality, overflow at 320px.
contract: Preserve Milestone, MilestoneProgressProps and the named MilestoneProgress export. current is a host-owned positional index; notify the clicked index synchronously and retain the actual host position until it changes.

Clamp finite indices to the collection and normalize invalid values to zero. A position equal to steps.length means complete. Empty collections retain a zero progress value and written no-milestones state.
Keep a native progressbar with finite 0-100 bounds, an accurate rounded percentage and a written current-stage detail. The visual completion fill follows the exact fraction in both directions.

Key stage rows by stable unique IDs so reordering retains focus. Use native buttons, Enter/Space activation, visible focus and at least 3:1 circle boundaries. Rows without a navigation handler are non-interactive.
Use separate heading IDs for independent instances. Support empty/arriving stages, completed workflows and long labels/details without document overflow.
The host owns milestone completion and persistence. Stage navigation is not a save, approval or completion operation.
